learningObjective: Explain the paged KV cache abstraction used by vLLM's PagedAttention and its motivation.

canonicalClaims.claim: PagedAttention stores KV in fixed-size physical blocks; each sequence has a block table mapping logical positions to physical blocks. Motivation: eliminate external fragmentation and internal reservation waste caused by pre-allocating each sequence's full max-length KV, and enable prefix/beam sharing.
conditions: Attention kernel is aware of the block table.
nonImplications: Does not imply zero indirection overhead.
Does not imply the block size is universal.

misconceptions.claim: Paged KV cache uses a hash table for random access.
misconceptions.whyWrong: It uses a per-sequence block table (an array), analogous to OS page tables.

misconceptions.claim: Paging refers to quantization block granularity, not memory layout.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Paging is a memory-management technique; unrelated to quantization.

misconceptions.claim: PagedAttention allocates each sequence's full max-length KV contiguously up front.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The whole point is to avoid this reservation waste.

implementationFacts: Typical block size in vLLM: 16 tokens.
Block tables are small (one integer per block per sequence) and reside in HBM alongside KV blocks.
performanceScenarios: Prefix caching, beam-search sharing, and swap-to-CPU rely on the block indirection layer.
